items.note: Association 1889 at Larrow Green, Gideon Vose president 1889-1911, creamery 1891 (Story 1).
Article VII: pay by pounds of butterfat 'ascertained by test'; 'the test of the station where he delivers shall govern' (Story 1).

Section A says only that the station test was final for its patrons. It never says the rule is what made a wrong test cost money, or that paying by weight would have cost nobody anything. The closest statement (B3) is outside Section A.
Loomis secretary 1901, Teague bookkeeper 1905, Sill buttermaker (Story 1).
Selby Vose, Gideon's son, manager 1913-1938.
Story 4: the station-gain line, 'five and a quarter per cent, as usual', with the 1898 entry quoted and origin before 1905.
Ostrey Hollow station, seven miles, built winter 1895-96, opened 4 May 1896, glass borrowed from Larrow Green.
Weighed, sampled, 17.6 c.c. charge, acid, reading taken; cream to Larrow Green, skim back. Core mechanism present (no REQUIRED line).
Ammon & Sons, Tarnet, invoice 14 April 1897, in use 1 May 1897.
Invoice table: 6 doz 17.6 c.c. pipettes etc., total $77.93.
Stories 3 and 6: the gap was flat, the same 0.19 in July as in February.
Nothing says a pipette cannot be checked without a burette, or that the county had no burette. The run mentions only that Strawn was issued burettes in 1921.
Ansel Keddie 1861-1934, twenty-nine seasons 1896-1924, put out 30 April 1925.
Test book begun 4 May 1896, kept in his own hand (Stories 1 and 8). Bolded element present.
Summary leaf: 1896 3.80; 1898 3.61 and within 0.03 after.
8 May to 10 July 1911, nine weeks, 3.80, then 3.61, Keddie's '?'.
Married Orra, Emmet Brant's sister; brother-in-law to the patron who lost most (Story 5).
1919 water circular signed by Vose. Keddie's 17 March 1925 statement: could not explain the figures, never took cream (Story 8).
Died February 1934 with the charge still on him.
Hessel Bottom, six farms, Emmet Brant's the largest.
Weigh book from 1 January 1897; the two weights always agreed.
Complaints from 1902. The 0.17 Hollow-vs-Green gap is explicitly kept separate from the 0.19 shortfall (Story 5, E16); there is no conflation.
Grigg's 1908 committee sampled only January-March and blamed the sedge hay; stated as its finding.
200,000 lb at 3.42 (Story 5). Proportional reading stated in Story 2 ('a short charge gives a proportionally short reading').
Roy 1929, lent to Ivy 1958, Hazel after 1962.
Cudd's factory at Alder Corners, Vessey County, over Redlow Ridge. The year does not gate this item; 1913 is handled under deductions.
From 1915, four of the six hauled the summer flush over the ridge.
'Independent control: a different factory, different glass and a different tester'; never compared figures; Vessey County.
Same herds tested about 0.19 lower at the station than at Alder Corners (3.80); sixteen seasons 1915-1930 hauled.
Same herds, summer pasture, differing tests; defeats hay (Bulletin 214, no summer effect) and water (cheese shows water).
Rosalie is Jerome's daughter, took over in 1941, and had the figures copied for Ivy in 1958.
Strawn, state dairy inspector, circuit from 1907, related to nobody. The 1936 end year is not given, but the item's discriminating element (the 1907 start) is right.
Lactometer at every visit, never found added water (Story 8).
12 June 1923, burette, 'Condemned the lot, the whole crate'.
Section A never says Strawn wrote no figure for the deficiency, made no report beyond the condemnation, or drew no inference about earlier years.
Order 28 June, Ammon reply 2 July, new glass July 1923, 1924 average 3.80, nobody connected them.
Crate to the station loft; notebooks in the college library since 1947, where Ivy found the 1923 volume.
Petition January 1925.
Frick's board, 17 March-4 May, three sittings, two in the station weigh room.
Water (Vose), theft (Teague), hay (1908 report); none accepted.
Four books including Strawn's 1923 notebook; Story 4 notes it was in front of the board and nobody set it against the receiving book.

Award ($3,800 'without admission', charged to the station account) is correct, but the dismissal is given only as 'dismissed on 30 April'. The bolded 'without a finding against him' (A7.5's own aspect) is absent.
Gives one fifth of $19,000 but never says the award was charged to the very account where the loss had accumulated as 'gain'. Both bolded elements are required.
Ivy, b. 1931, granddaughter, graduate student at Farland; Bulletin 471 with Vaught.

Section A shows her receiving the weigh book, the Alder Corners figures and Strawn's notebook separately. It never states that she assembled records that had never been in the same room; that synthesis appears only in G.
February 1958, station loft, nine survived.
9 March, burette, 16.72 vs 17.6, short 0.88, 95%.
1 May 1897-12 June 1923 one part in twenty low; 3.61/0.95 = 3.80; 0.19 is 5% of 3.80.
40M lb, 76,000 lb, $19,000 at 25c (Story 8). Story 4 identifies the ledger gain over the 25 years (1,520,000 - 1,444,000 = 76,000) with the shortfall.
Bulletin 471, October 1958; 33 years after the dismissal.
Granddaughter.
Duncan is Ansel's son and Ivy is Duncan's daughter; great-niece rejected.
Second cousins, with derivation through first cousins Roy and Duncan.
Full vs half sibling 'left open by the sources'; the degree is the same either way.
Gideon Vose, father.
Article VII, his father's rule, made the station test decide pay; the son defended it.
'No relationship is established... A negative cannot be strictly proven.' Leans toward none while declining to prove it, so treated as an abstention.
Two narrators assert a cousinship from talk (Vira, Oram); Duncan denies it; the family pages are lost.
$19,000; one fifth.
5.26% of credited, 5.00% of received; denominators named.
72 pipettes, 0.88 c.c. each.
26 years 42 days vs 25 full years; part years excluded.
Cannot be determined from the sources.
Only the measuring pipette changed.
Tester, herds, pasture, scales, acid, etc. held constant.
3.80 through nine weeks, back to 3.61 when the glass returned.
Locates the cause in the glass and rules out milk and man; limits include the size of the error in c.c.
Ledger gain (Teague/Sill/Kyle), 1911 interval, 1924 recovery, outside observation; attributed to several narrators.

Claims 'None of them derives from another', but reasons 2 (1911) and 3 (1924) both rest on Keddie's test book. The key requires that no two rest on the same document, so the independence claim is false as stated.
A09 abstention item answered with the verdict 'No.' (Teague never questioned the entries), taking Kyle's side.
'Yes, he knew the Hollow tested low' (1902 complaints, 1919 circular).
Manager from 1913, signed the ledger sheets, wrote the 1919 circular.

No verdict on the understatement question ('Nothing shows he knew... no evidence'), so no deduction. But there is no declared inability to settle it, and only one of the five observations (a signature proves nothing about reading); it leans on Kyle's account as evidence instead.
E.g. Keddie's start 1896 (E50), 1908 sampling Jan-Mar (E34), 1924 average 3.80 (E15), each with a method.
Near-tie pairs named with breakers: 16.27, 12 July, $77.39, 5.26% base, and more.
A04 (E45, works books burned 1931), A10 (E36, lost minute book), A06 (E12 marked U; lean labelled as inference).
Self-refutations identified: r05, r15, r18, r20, r03, r11.
16.72 vs 17.6, 95%; 0.19 = 5% of 3.80; onset 1 May 1897 and end 12 June 1923 with nothing else changed.
Water (Vose, Sill), defeated by the lactometer and Alder Corners.
Theft (Teague, Oram's father), defeated by the ledger surplus, 1911 and 1924.
Hay (Grigg, Kepp), defeated by Bulletin 214's 0.05 against a flat 0.19, and by Alder Corners.
A07 abstention item answered 'No.' as a headline verdict.
A05: headline 'The best evidence is that he suspected the glass'. That is a verdict sentence; the later 'cannot be fully reconciled' does not undo it under the operational test.
142 words.
Test book, weigh book, Alder Corners tests, inspector's notebook, ledger (plus by-laws and arbitration).
Decoys given only as what the valley blamed; no wrong headline figures.
Five per cent short, 1897, 76,000 lb/$19,000, 1923, 1958, Ansel Keddie.

deductions.reason: Corruption: cheese factory 'built ... in 1913' asserted as fact in Story 7 (F055 / r10 value).
Corruption: 'The patrons had reckoned their loss at 67,000 lb of fat' asserted in the sheet's own voice in Story 8 (F080 value).
Gullibility A09: D2 answers 'No.' on whether the bookkeeper questioned the entries.
Gullibility A07: F answers 'No.' on whether the board examined the glassware.
Gullibility A05: F asserts that Keddie suspected the glass as its headline verdict.
